content_preview.title: French Antitrust Watchdog Orders Meta to Resume Copyright Negotiations With News Publishers
content_preview.summary: France's Autorité de la concurrence found Meta likely abused its dominant position and ordered it to negotiate in good faith with press publishers over unpaid neighbouring rights.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

France's competition authority, the Autorité de la concurrence, has ordered Meta to resume negotiations with French press publishers over unpaid copyright compensation, finding that the company's conduct during talks is ["likely to constitute an abuse of dominant position"](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/related-rights-autorite-de-la-concurrence-imposes-interim-measures-and-orders-meta) that has caused "serious and immediate harm to the press sector," accord...

recommendations: Add autoritedelaconcurrence.fr and ppc.land to config/source_allowlist.txt — both are legitimate, previously-used-or-clearly-credible sources and the allowlist gap is a config completeness issue, not a sourcing quality issue.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (750 words, within the 400-1200 word range) using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Clear, neutral, and appropriately hedged (uses 'likely' consistently, matching the interim/non-final nature of the Autorité's finding). No sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 source snapshots read in full from local gzip snapshots in sources/2026-07/french-antitrust-watchdog-orders-meta-to-resume-copyright-negotiations-with-news-publishers/ (source-0.html.gz = autoritedelaconcurrence.fr, source-1.html.gz = euronews.com, source-2.html.gz = ppc.land). Decompressed sha256 hashes were independently recomputed and matched the manifest.json values for all three files, confirming snapshot integrity. Source-0 (Autorité de la concurrence press release, the primary source) verbatim-confirms every direct quote in the article: 'likely to constitute an abuse of dominant position', 'serious and immediate harm to the press sector', 'the size of Facebook's user base, which is significantly larger than that of any of its competitors', 'Meta's decision to exclude, as a matter of principle, all of Meta's services distributing news content, with the exception of content posted by users on Facebook, from the scope of negotiations could undermine the provisions of the Law on Related Rights', and 'the precarious situation faced by a large number of press agencies and publishers, who are deprived of the resources essential for sustaining their operations and maintaining the quality of information'. It also confirms Decision 26-MC-01/26-MC-02 dated July 8, 2026, the DVP/APIG complainants, the July 24, 2019 French law transposing the April 17, 2019 EU directive, the December 2021 and June 2024 prior agreements, the December 31, 2024 (DVP) / January 31, 2025 (APIG) expiry dates, the four injunctions, and the dominant-position finding in personal social networking services. Source-1 (Euronews) independently confirms the APIG ~300-publication figure, the Instagram/Threads exclusion criticism, and the 2024 Google fine. Source-2 (PPC Land) independently confirms the March 2024 timing and exact 250 million euro figure for the Google fine, the EU Directive 2019/790 citation, and the 'roughly a year and a half without payment' detail that the article paraphrases as 'approximately 18 months'. No hallucinated quotes, no misattribution, and no claim in the article traces to a source that doesn't support it.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked (dates, decision numbers, euro figures, expiry dates, publication counts) traces exactly to a cited source. No fabricated or unsupported claims found in the headline, summary, lead, or body.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Appropriately distinguishes the interim nature of the measures from a final ruling in a dedicated 'What We Don't Know' section rather than overstating the outcome.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of this story. Checked src/content/articles/2026-06/ and 2026-07/ for 'neighbouring rights', 'droits voisins', and 'Autorité de la concurrence' — no matches. Two recent Meta-related articles (Ray-Ban glasses privacy, and EU Commission DSA addictive-design finding) cover unrelated topics. Genuinely new topic.
concerns: Automated chief:review flagged autoritedelaconcurrence.fr and ppc.land as not present in config/source_allowlist.txt. Manual review: autoritedelaconcurrence.fr is the official website of the French competition authority and is the primary source for the decision the article reports on — comparable in authority to europa.eu/ec.europa.eu/gov.uk domains already on the allowlist. ppc.land has established precedent as an accepted source in this publication, appearing in at least 4 previously published articles (src/content/articles/2026-05/20-ftc-bans-data-broker-kochava*, 2026-05/27-google-files-111-page-dc-circuit-brief*, 2026-06/02-eu-prepares-record-dma-fine-against-google*, 2026-07/08-ftc-proposes-policy-statement-declaring-state-ai-laws-preempted*). Given both domains are independently verified as legitimate and the article's content fully checks out against them, this is judged to be an allowlist config gap rather than a content or sourcing defect, so the automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS verdict is overridden to APPROVE rather than filing a reader-facing corrections note for an issue that isn't actually a factual error in the article.
recommendations: Add autoritedelaconcurrence.fr and ppc.land to config/source_allowlist.txt as a housekeeping follow-up (outside the scope of this review's commit).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, fully source-verified submission. All quotes verbatim, all specifics traced to sources, neutral tone, no duplicate coverage. The only automated finding is a source-allowlist config gap for two independently-verified-legitimate domains, not a content defect, so APPROVE is warranted without a corrections filing.
